title: Hearing a chart first time and recording Walk on the Wild Side
summary: Even Mancini got nervous hearing his work; in 2004 John made his own CD because there was no place for his music.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So you based most of your life on the fact that you had this urge, you heard something in your head, you wrote it down and you waited for someone to play it.
There’s nothing like hearing the chart the first time, is there?

It’s amazing. Mancini told me that no matter how many times that he’s written for orchestra or big band or films or whatever, he always got nervous when he got on that podium to hear what it really sounded like. He knew what it was going to sound like, but to hear, to have that experience. It’s great. You say wow, this is fantastic. And of course now I have to spend my money to hear it played because there are no big bands to write for anymore.

Yeah well that’s it. You know that’s what prompted me in 2004 I did that “Walk on the Wild Side” CD. I figured I wrote for everybody else, now I’m going to write for me. You know I’m going to write for me and have something out there with my name on it finally. I didn’t mind being second fiddle to the leader of the band, not at all. But there was no
place to go with my music, I mean, really. And writing for publishing or for the educational field, that’s not the same and you don’t really get to hear it played.
